| D-26.1 | §26.1 | HIST | **Internal:** `Logger` handle (owned ident, explicit facility), with an optional structured journald protocol. **Boundary:** the global logger keeps the ident *by pointer*, as the contract says. The connection is synchronised (observable, stricter). |
| D-26.2 | §26.1 | HIST, ARB | **syslog (phase 13); decisions.** `liella::log::Logger` (owned ident, options, facility, mask, channels); the global logger `legacy::log_compat::GLOBAL` keeps the ident by pointer under one lock over settings, connection and delivery; a fork child resets the lock and shares the connection. **Never blocks indefinitely:** sends use `MSG_DONTWAIT\|MSG_NOSIGNAL` and `ppoll` with at most 1 s per message, and the console is opened `O_NONBLOCK` with the same bound (the reference blocks on a full receiver or a FIFO console with no reader); a timeout counts as not delivered (`LOG_CONS` then writes to the console). One reconnect and resend on any other failure. The socket is moved to descriptor 3 or above. The stream transport cuts the text at the first NUL. `errno` is never changed (X3; the reference leaks it after a failed send). A NULL format logs nothing (the reference crashes). Kept from the reference: the extra "unknown facility/priority" record for stray priority bits, `openlog` replacing the options, facility 0 accepted, `closelog` resetting only the ident, `setlogmask(0)` querying; timestamp per `localtime_r`, English month names; console form `IDENT[PID]: MSG\r\n`. The journald protocol of D-26.1 is not built (optional). `openlog(NULL)` selects the program name, also after an earlier `openlog` with another ident (openlog(3); owner ruling 2026-10-04; the reference keeps the previous ident: recorded in `syslog_products`). |

| D-27.4 | §27 | — | **`dl_iterate_phdr`** (static programs, until the loader of phase 14 supplies the object list): one callback for the main program (name "", `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`, `dlpi_addr` from `PT_PHDR`, TLS module 1 and the calling thread's block when `PT_TLS` exists), then one for the vDSO (`linux-vdso.so.1`, ELF64 header fields e_phoff at 32, e_phentsize 54, e_phnum 56) when `AT_SYSINFO_EHDR` is set, as a glibc static program reports (probe); `dlpi_adds` = objects, `dlpi_subs` = 0, `size` = 64; a non-zero callback result stops the walk and is returned; it reads immutable startup data only (async-signal-safe). **`stime`** is compat-only as in glibc 2.39: `libc.so` exports `stime@GLIBC_2.2.5` (non-default; `.symver` stub in `s23_time.rs`, listed in the version script by `cargo xtask so`), `libc.a` offers no plain `stime`, so no new program links it while old binaries resolve it. Known difference: `libc.so` binds `dl_iterate_phdr` GLOBAL where glibc binds WEAK (the same for every WEAK export, e.g. `fgetc`). Probes: CONF-SYMS-2. |
| D-27.5 | §27.1 | — | **`_dl_find_object`** (static programs, until phase 14): a `pc` in one of the main program's `PT_LOAD` segments gives that segment's range (a static glibc 2.39 program reports the segment, not the whole object), one in the vDSO the vDSO's whole mapped range; `dlfo_eh_frame` = the object's `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` address (0 without one), `dlfo_flags` 0, result 0; any other `pc` (stack, past `_end`, 0) gives -1 and leaves `*result` alone. libgcc_eh (GCC 13) calls it, so a static C++ or `-fexceptions` program needs it to link. Exported with feature `runtime` only (`export! { runtime ... }`): the answer covers only a process Liella started, so test builds that interpose exports on a host process keep the host's (interposed, it hid the host's shared objects from Rust's panic unwinder: SIGABRT). Known gap: `dlfo_link_map` is 0 (no `struct link_map` before phase 14; glibc gives a non-null one). Probe: PTHREAD-ONCE-UNWIND-2 (static and dynamic glibc). |
| D-27.6 | §27.5 | — | **`__x86_get_cpuid_feature_leaf@GLIBC_2.33`** (`<sys/platform/x86.h>`, behind `CPU_FEATURE_PRESENT`/`CPU_FEATURE_ACTIVE`): returns `struct cpuid_feature` (32 bytes, align 4: the raw CPUID words eax, ebx, ecx, edx, then the "active" words in that order). Index to leaf: 0=1, 1=7.0, 2=0x80000001, 3=0xd.1, 4=0x80000007, 5=0x80000008, 6=7.1, 7=0x19, 8=0x14.0, 9=0x24. A leaf or subleaf past the CPU's maximum reads zero. Index 10 and above (including 0xffffffff) gets one shared all-zero entry, never NULL. The table is filled on the first call (`liella_rt::cpu::feature_leaves`). Active = present AND a fixed per-bit rule: the `ACTIVE_ALWAYS` bits; FMA/AVX/F16C/AVX2 only with XCR0 SSE+AVX state; AVX-512 F/DQ/CD/BW/VL only with XCR0 0xe6; HLE/RTM inactive and RTM_ALWAYS_ABORT active (even though not present) when 7.EDX bit 11 or 13 is set. Probe: X86-CPUID-FEATURE-LEAF (glibc 2.39 on Skylake-SP host Skylake-SP, Haswell-EP host Haswell, Broadwell-EP host Broadwell, Zen 1 host). **Known gaps (ruling #778, #781, #782):** (1) an active bit never seen present on a probed CPU stays inactive (AVX512_IFMA/VBMI/VNNI/BITALG, GFNI, VAES, VPCLMULQDQ, the 7.1, 0x19, 0x14 and 0x24 active bits, among others). This is the safe answer: a feature is never claimed usable when it is not. Trigger: extend `ACTIVE_ALWAYS` once a newer CPU (Ice Lake+ / Zen 4) can be probed against glibc. (2) The TSX rule (abort bit 11 or 13) rests on one CPU per side (Skylake-SP host with bit 13, Broadwell-EP host without either bit). A model-based rule cannot be told apart on these hosts. (3) `glibc.cpu.hwcaps` tunable masking of the active bits is not implemented. |
| D-27.7 | §27 | SEC | **The loader's ELF reader (`liella_ld::elf`, IP-24 part 1, DL-ELF-READ-1): error rules.** Input is a byte slice; no I/O, no allocation, no panic, no read outside the slice; every offset, count and size is checked with checked arithmetic (threat-model rule 4). `Elf::parse::<A: Arch>` checks, in this order, and returns the first failure as a typed `ElfError`: length >= 64 (`TooShort`); magic; `EI_CLASS` = `A::EI_CLASS` = ELFCLASS64 (`WrongClass`, s27_1_f_0); `EI_DATA` = `A::EI_DATA` (`WrongData`; fields are decoded in that byte order); `EI_VERSION` = 1; `EI_OSABI` System V or GNU; `e_type` `ET_EXEC` or `ET_DYN`; `e_machine` = `A::E_MACHINE` (identity only through `liella_ld::arch`, design §0a); `e_version` = 1; `e_ehsize` = 64; `e_phnum` != `PN_XNUM` (section headers are never read); `e_phentsize` = 56 unless `e_phnum` = 0; the program header table inside the slice and not overlapping the ELF header; then per program header in index order: `p_offset + p_filesz` and `p_vaddr + p_memsz` do not overflow, `p_align` 0 or a power of two, `PT_LOAD` `p_filesz <= p_memsz`, the file ranges of `PT_DYNAMIC`/`PT_INTERP`/`PT_NOTE` overlap neither the ELF header nor the table, at most one `PT_DYNAMIC` and one `PT_INTERP`. Segment contents are checked when read (the slice may be a file prefix): a range outside the slice is `OutOfRange`; `PT_INTERP` is a non-empty path with exactly one NUL, at the end; `PT_DYNAMIC` is a multiple of 16 bytes and holds a `DT_NULL` (entries after the first `DT_NULL` are never read); `DT_STRTAB` and `DT_STRSZ` at most once each, both or neither, and both when a string-valued tag (`DT_NEEDED`, `DT_SONAME`, `DT_RPATH`, `DT_RUNPATH`) is present; the string table lies wholly in the file-backed part of one `PT_LOAD` (`AddressNotMapped`); a string offset is below `DT_STRSZ` and its NUL inside the table. Notes are padded to 8 when `p_align` is 8 and to 4 when it is 0-4 (any other value is `BadNoteAlign`); a note header, name or descriptor past the segment end is `NoteTruncated`, a non-empty name without a final NUL `BadNoteName`; `NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0` properties are 8-aligned and a property past its descriptor is `PropertyTruncated`. Iterators yield `Result` and stop after the first error. Semantic segment checks (order, congruence, overlap of `PT_LOAD`s) belong to the mapper (§3); dlerror texts wait for the M14-0/DL-0b probes. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/elf_reader.rs` (malformed corpus), `elf_readelf_parity.rs` (readelf -h/-l/-d/-n). |
| D-27.8 | §27 | SEC | **The loader's ELF reader, part 2 (`liella_ld::elf`, IP-24 part 2, DL-ELF-READ-2): hash tables, versions, relocation iterators.** Same input rules as D-27.7 (no I/O, allocation, panic or read outside the slice; checked arithmetic; iterators yield one error and stop). Tables are found through `Dynamic`: a part-2 tag occurs at most once (`DuplicateDynamic`); address/size pairs (`DT_RELA`/`RELASZ`, `DT_JMPREL`/`PLTRELSZ`, `DT_RELR`/`RELRSZ`, `DT_VERDEF`/`VERDEFNUM`, `DT_VERNEED`/`VERNEEDNUM`) are both or neither (`MissingDynamic(tag)`); `DT_RELAENT` = 24 and `DT_RELRENT` = 8 are required with `DT_RELA`/`DT_RELR`, `DT_PLTREL` = `DT_RELA` with `DT_JMPREL` (`MissingDynamic`/`BadDynamicValue`); a size that is not whole entries is `TableSize`. Fixed-length tables (SysV hash header + `nbucket+nchain` words, GNU hash header + Bloom words + buckets, RELA, RELR) lie wholly in the file-backed part of one `PT_LOAD` (`AddressNotMapped`); tables walked to their end (GNU chain, verdef, verneed, versym) are read within the rest of that segment. GNU hash: at least one Bloom word and a shift below 64 (`BadHashHeader`); a bucket below `symoffset` or a chain past the mapped bytes is `HashIndex`. SysV: a bucket/chain value at or past `nchain` is `HashIndex`, a chain longer than `nchain` `HashChainLoop`; no buckets = empty. Symbol count: SysV `nchain`, else the end of the GNU chain from the highest bucket (all buckets empty: `symoffset`, a lower bound). Versions: revision 1 (`BadVersionRevision`); a chain ending (next 0) before its count is `VersionCount`, an entry past the segment `VersionTruncated`; names through the string rules of D-27.7; a `versym` index above the highest `vd_ndx`/`vna_other` (hidden bit masked) is `VersionIndex`, an entry past the mapping `SymbolIndex` (the count is a hint, not a bound). RELA entries are classified only through `Arch::classify` into `RelocKind`; an unknown type is `Unsupported(n)` and still yielded (design §0a); `TextRel` carries width, pc-relative and signed (32 vs 32S). RELR: an even entry is an address, an odd entry a 63-word bitmap after the previous address or bitmap; a bitmap with no address before it is `RelrNoBase`, an address past 2^64 `RelrOverflow`. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/elf_tables.rs`, `elf_readelf_parity.rs` (readelf -r/-V/--dyn-syms); fuzz target `elf` (docs/fuzzing.md). |
| D-27.9 | §22, §27 | — | **The placeholder libraries (DL-1 `DL-PLACEHOLDERS`, design §16, R14-12).** `cargo xtask so` builds `libpthread.so.0`, `libdl.so.2`, `librt.so.1`, `libutil.so.1`, `libanl.so.1` and `libc_malloc_debug.so.0` from `spec/abi/versions.tsv` (`xtask/src/placeholders.rs`), each with its soname and `DT_NEEDED libc.so.6`. **Rule:** a library's version nodes are the versions of its rows (numeric order, each the parent of the next, no `GLIBC_PRIVATE`); it exports each of its rows whose name `libc.so.6` has no row for, at the row's version and binding; every other name is reached through `libc.so.6` and never defined twice. So the five placeholders export only their `__lib<x>_version_placeholder` versions (bodies return), and `libc_malloc_debug.so.0` only `malloc_get_state`/`malloc_set_state` (bodies in `crates/libc-so/placeholders/libc_malloc_debug.c`: NULL / -1 with `ENOSYS`, as `libc.a`'s, D-3.5) while defining all its nodes; preloading it gives no hooks. An export without a body is a build error. Empty `libdl.a`, `librt.a`, `libutil.a`, `libanl.a` (and `libpthread.a`) let `-static -l<x>` resolve. **Check:** each built library is read back with `readelf` and compared with the table independently of the generator (soname, `DT_NEEDED`, version definitions, every defined export: unversioned, another library's row, a `libc.so.6` name, a missing row are errors), and no shared product (`libc.so.6`, `libm.so.6` included) defines or exports `GLIBC_PRIVATE` (R14-12). Tests: `placeholders::tests` (xtask), `s22_n_1` (links `-lpthread -ldl -lrt -lutil -lanl` statically and runs; dynamically, links only until DL-14). |
| D-27.10 | §1.1, §27 | SEC | **The self-relocator** (DL-BOOT-RELOC, phase 14 DL-4, ruling R14-1 option (a), design §1): logic in `liella_ld::boot` (pure, host-tested), memory views in `boundary/src/bootstrap.rs` (category *slice*). First user: the static-PIE start of `libc.a` (closes phase-4 deviation 2); `ld.so` reuses it (DL-5). Rules: (1) the image is found through its own ELF header, `__ehdr_start` declared hidden and NOT weak in a C file of its own (`csys/src/adapter/image_anchor.c`, helper `liella_link_image_header`), so the compiler takes its address with one RIP-relative instruction; every reference made before pass 1 ends must be PC-relative like this (a weak reference compiles to a GOT load, and the GOT is unrelocated: DL-BOOT-RELOC's first `_DYNAMIC` anchor crashed every static PIE). `cargo xtask so` checks that the anchor's archive member references `__ehdr_start` and has no GOT-typed relocation. A static PIE links the start object `liella-rcrt1.o` (`entry.S` assembled with `-DLIELLA_STATIC_PIE`; its `_start` calls `liella_start_main_static_pie`, PC-relative, checked by `cargo xtask so`), which runs `runtime::start::<true>`; `liella-crt1.o` runs `start::<false>`, which compiles no relocation step and no type test (DL-BOOT-RELOC-3: no static non-PIE start pays for static PIE). The relocating start still relocates only when the header's `e_type` is `ET_DYN`; bias = the header's run-time address minus the `p_vaddr` of the `PT_LOAD` at file offset 0, and `PT_DYNAMIC` is found at bias + its `p_vaddr` (a static PIE from GNU ld has no `PT_PHDR`, so the header bias reads 0; the TLS image and RELRO range are moved by the real bias). (2) It needs one `PT_DYNAMIC` and exactly one writable `PT_LOAD`; every target lies in that segment (8 bytes inside it), every table (`DT_RELA`, `DT_JMPREL`, `DT_RELR`) holds whole entries and lies outside it; `DT_TEXTREL`, `DT_RELAENT` not 24, `DT_RELRENT` not 8, `DT_PLTREL` not `DT_RELA`, a missing `DT_NULL`, a RELR bitmap before an address or an address overflow are refused. (3) Pass 1, before any relocated data is read: `DT_RELA` then `DT_JMPREL` entries of kind `RelocKind::Relative` (through `Arch::classify`, never a raw type number) get bias + addend, then each RELR address gets += bias; `Irelative` and `None` wait; any other kind is refused. A refusal in pass 1 writes one fixed line to fd 2 and exits 127 (nothing that reads relocated data may run). (4) Pass 2, where the non-PIE start applies `.rela.iplt` (after the CPU paths, before the constructors and before RELRO is protected): each `Irelative` entry of both tables calls its resolver at bias + addend and stores the result; the segment view is made after the resolver returns. No panics anywhere in the relocator (a `Location` is relocated data). (5) `xtask so` makes `DW.ref.rust_eh_personality` weak hidden in the product crate's own `libc.a` objects (it was LOCAL in a COMDAT group, so a PIE link refused the other members' references). Tests: `liella_ld::boot` unit tests; `conformance/c/s01_static_pie.c` (RELR) and `s01_static_pie_rela.c` (RELA), each with an IFUNC called and taken by address, a pointer in the TLS image, a constructor and 100 starts (50 randomised, 50 `ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE`); plants `handoff/DL-BOOT-RELOC-plants.txt`. |
| D-27.11 | §27.1 | — | **Symbol lookup (`liella_ld::symbols`, phase 14 DL-9, DL-SYMBOLS).** Pure logic over the reader (no I/O, allocation or panic; malformed tables give a typed `LookupError`). The reader gains `Dynamic::symtab` (`DT_SYMENT`, when present, must be 24; an index at or past the hash-table symbol count is `SymbolIndex`). **Hashes:** gABI SysV hash and the GNU hash (`h*33+c` from 5381); an object is searched through its GNU table when it has one (Bloom check, then chain entries whose hash matches with bit 0 ignored), else SysV; both give the same answers. **Definitions:** defined (`st_shndx` not `SHN_UNDEF`), binding GLOBAL/WEAK/GNU_UNIQUE, type NOTYPE/OBJECT/FUNC/COMMON/TLS/GNU_IFUNC, visibility not HIDDEN/INTERNAL, versym index not 0. **Versions** (probe-settled, spec/behaviour/dynlink.md "Symbol binding"): an unversioned relocation reference (versym 0/1 or no versym) binds the definition with the lowest version index, hidden or not (base first, then the oldest version); a lookup by name alone (`dlsym`) binds base or default (not hidden) definitions only; a named version (`vna_other` resolved to its name, `dlvsym`) binds exactly that version, hidden or not, never a base (index 1) definition; in an object without `versym` every definition matches every request (the lookup stays permissive: a program that needs a version from an object without version tables is REFUSED like the reference loader, exit 127 and a message naming the object and the version, with no warn-and-continue and no COMPAT option; that refusal belongs to the load-time version check, DL-10 in the plan, not to the lookup; coordinator ruling #3655). Names are compared as bytes, no node is special (`LIELLA_PRIVATE` included, R14-12). **Scopes** (design §5): global; global then the dlopen group (local first with `RTLD_DEEPBIND`); `RTLD_NEXT` = after the caller in the global scope, else in its local scope; a COPY lookup excludes the program. **Binding:** the first object in scope order that defines the name wins, weak or strong (probe: link order decides, `LD_DYNAMIC_WEAK=1` changes nothing); an undefined weak reference binds 0, an undefined strong one is `Undefined`; an `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` definition is replaced by the namespace registry's entry for (name, version name), or recorded there (probe: shared across two `RTLD_LOCAL` dlopens). Version names are found by walking `DT_VERDEF` per lookup (a per-object index is the L14-7 memo, later). |

| D-29.1 | §29 | HIST, COMPAT | RPC and XDR follow RFC 5531/4506. NIS follows the YP protocol. STREAMS and removed interfaces are `ENOSYS` stubs. `_IO_*` vtable objects export tables of our functions (F32). |
| D-29.2 | §29.1 | COMPAT | **UDP RPC replies from the called address only** (owner ruling 2026-10-23, #1643, provisional): the UDP client compares each datagram's `recvfrom` source (port and IPv4 address) with the called address and drops any other, whatever its xid; the socket is not connected (that would change ICMP error reporting). A reply-shaped datagram (type REPLY, status accepted or denied; the xid is never consulted) from another address during a call turns its timeout into `RPC_CANTRECV` with `EREMCHG`; nothing ends a call early. Each call's xid is fresh random bits (`getrandom`), except the call after `CLSET_XID`, which is stepped from the set value as probed. Opt-out COMPAT-12 (`liella.compat.rpc_reply_any_source=1`, ignored when `AT_SECURE`). `clnt_broadcast` and TCP are not affected. Reason: replies over UDP are matched by xid only; accepting them from any source lets a third party who can send packets to the client answer in the server's place. **Superseded by D-29.5** (the UDP client is a failing stub; COMPAT-12 withdrawn). |
| D-29.3 | §29.4 | COMPAT | **`<regexp.h>` `step`/`advance` are stubs; `malloc_get_state`/`malloc_set_state` stay failing stubs** (owner rulings R6 and R9, 2026-11-04, SCOPE-APPLY-STUBS). `step` and `advance` return 0 (no match) for every argument and never write `loc1`, `loc2` or `locs`; the three objects stay exported, so old binaries still link. LG-10 (the matcher) is deferred until the LG-19 corpus finds a user. `malloc_get_state` returns NULL and `malloc_set_state` returns -1, both with `errno` ENOSYS (D-3.5, unchanged); `mtrace`/`muntrace` are unchanged. No compatibility option: the interfaces are obsolete and the old matcher is not offered (recorded in the differences row). |
| D-29.4 | §29.1 | COMPAT, SEC | **Secure-RPC authentication, the key server client and the DES API are failing stubs** (owner ruling 2026-10-27; supersedes the LG-16 DES/netname behaviour of D-29.1 and ruling #1675): insecure by design, and outside the public API of glibc since 2.32. Each name stays exported at its compat version (an old program loads); no restore option (security). Failure table: `ecb_crypt`/`cbc_crypt` `DESERR_HWERROR` (2), buffer untouched; `des_setparity` no effect; `passwd2des` no effect (key untouched); `xencrypt`/`xdecrypt`, `key_secretkey_is_set`, `getpublickey`, `getsecretkey`, `authdes_getucred`, `user2netname`, `host2netname`, `getnetname`, `netname2user`, `netname2host` `0`; `key_setsecret`, `key_gendes`, `key_encryptsession[_pk]`, `key_decryptsession[_pk]`, `key_get_conv`, `key_setnet` `-1`; `authdes_create`, `authdes_pk_create`, `authunix_create[_default]` `NULL`. Every stub sets `errno` to `EOPNOTSUPP` and touches no network, file or key server. Test: `crates/boundary/tests/s29_rpc_auth_stubs.rs`. Still to do (same ruling): the client/server/portmapper constructors and calls (NULL + `rpc_createerr` `RPC_SYSTEMERROR`/`EOPNOTSUPP`), the rcmd family (`-1`, `EOPNOTSUPP`), `libnsl.so.1` stubs, code removal, COMPAT-12 withdrawal. |
| D-29.5 | §29.1 | COMPAT, SEC | **The ONC RPC client, port mapper calls and server are failing stubs** (owner rulings R13 and 2026-10-27; the client/server item of D-29.4; supersedes D-29.2 and the LG-14/LG-15 behaviour of D-29.1; LEGACY-RPC-CLNT-SVC-STUBS). Each name stays exported at its compat version, and the 17 not exported before (`clnt_create`, `clntraw_create`, `clntunix_create`, `callrpc`, `clnt_broadcast`, `pmap_set`, `pmap_unset`, `pmap_getmaps`, `pmap_rmtcall`, `getrpcport`, `get_myaddress`, `rtime`, `registerrpc`, `svcraw_create`, `svcunix_create`, `svcunixfd_create`, `svcudp_enablecache`) are now exported as stubs, so an old program loads. Every stub sets `errno` `EOPNOTSUPP` and opens, reads, writes or closes no descriptor (a caller's `*sockp` and socket untouched), contacts no port mapper and keeps no memory. Failure table: the client and transport constructors (`clnt_create`, `clntudp_create`, `clntudp_bufcreate`, `clnttcp_create`, `clntunix_create`, `clntraw_create`, `svcudp_create`, `svcudp_bufcreate`, `svctcp_create`, `svcfd_create`, `svcraw_create`, `svcunix_create`, `svcunixfd_create`), `authnone_create` and `pmap_getmaps` `NULL`; `callrpc`, `clnt_broadcast`, `pmap_rmtcall` `RPC_SYSTEMERROR` (outputs untouched); `pmap_getport`, `getrpcport`, `pmap_set`, `pmap_unset`, `svc_register`, `svc_sendreply`, `svcudp_enablecache` `0`; `registerrpc`, `rtime` `-1`; `_authenticate` `AUTH_FAILED`; `get_myaddress`, `xprt_register`, `xprt_unregister`, `svc_unregister`, `svcerr_*`, `svc_getreq*`, `svc_exit` no effect; `svc_run` returns at once; `_seterr_reply` stores `RPC_SYSTEMERROR`/`EOPNOTSUPP` in its `rpc_err`. Every client-side stub and every constructor also sets `rpc_createerr` to `RPC_SYSTEMERROR` with `re_errno` `EOPNOTSUPP`, which `clnt_spcreateerror` prints. Kept: `__rpc_thread_createerr` (per thread), the `clnt_*err` printers, `__rpc_thread_svc_fdset` (always empty), `bindresvport` (D-15.7), `_rpc_dtablesize`. COMPAT-12 withdrawn and the tunable `liella.compat.rpc_reply_any_source` no longer read. No restore option (security, as D-29.4). Not exported yet (internal names, no documented contract): `__libc_clntudp_bufcreate`, `__rpc_thread_svc_pollfd`, `__rpc_thread_svc_max_pollfd`. Test: `crates/boundary/tests/s29_rpc_clnt_svc_stubs.rs`. |
| D-29.6 | §29.2, §27 | COMPAT, SEC | **`libnsl.so.1` is a placeholder of failing NIS/YP and NIS+ stubs** (owner rulings R13 and 2026-10-27, LG-17/LG-18 re-scope; D-27.9's machinery; LEGACY-RPC-LIBNSL-PLACEHOLDER). `cargo xtask so` builds it like the D-27.9 placeholders: its version node and exports from `spec/abi/versions.tsv` (121 names, all `compat` at `GLIBC_2.2.5`, so only an already-linked program binds them; the 6 `GLIBC_PRIVATE` rows are left out, R14-12), `DT_NEEDED libc.so.6`, checked by `product_errors`. No `libnsl.a` (versions.tsv has only `compat` rows, so no static link could use one). **Table-driven:** `crates/libc-so/placeholders/libnsl.tsv` has one row per export (kind and value); `placeholders::stub_bodies` generates each C body from it and refuses a table that misses an export or names a non-export; the test reads the same table. Every stub returns at once and opens, reads or writes no descriptor, socket or file, starts no thread and keeps no memory. **Values** (from black-box probes of the reference with no NIS domain, `ypbind` or NIS+ cold-start file, so a program sees what it sees there): `yp_bind` `YPERR_YPBIND` (10), `yp_get_default_domain` `YPERR_NODOM` (12), `yp_first` `YPERR_RPC` (2), `yp_all` `YPERR_DOMAIN` (3), `yp_match`, `yp_next`, `yp_order`, `yp_master`, `yp_maplist`, `yp_update` `YPERR_YPERR` (6), `ypprot_err` 6, `__yp_check` 0; outputs are left untouched; the NIS+ calls that return a result object (`nis_lookup`, `nis_list`, `nis_add`, `nis_remove`, `nis_modify`, the `_entry` forms, `nis_first_entry`, `nis_next_entry`, `nis_checkpoint`) a new 56-byte result with status `NIS_UNAVAIL` (41) and no objects (the reference's object size and status), freed by `nis_freeresult`; the `nis_error` calls (`nis_mkdir`, `nis_rmdir`, `nis_servstate`, `nis_stats`, the group calls but `nis_ismember`, `__nisbind_create`/`_connect`/`_next`) 41; `nis_ismember`, `nis_write_obj`, `writeColdStartFile`, every `xdr_*` 0 (`FALSE`); `nis_dir_cmp` `NOT_SEQUENTIAL` (3); `__nis_default_ttl`, `__nis_default_access`, `__nis_hash` 0; every other pointer (`nis_local_*`, `nis_leaf_of`/`nis_name_of`/`nis_domain_of` and their `_r` forms, `nis_getnames`, `nis_getservlist`, the `nis_clone_*`, `nis_read_obj`, `readColdStartFile`, `__nis_finddirectory`, `__nis_default_owner`/`_group`) `NULL` with `errno` `EOPNOTSUPP`. **Harmless choices** (no failure value exists): `yperr_string`, `ypbinderr_string`, `nis_sperrno`, `nis_sperror` return the text "NIS and NIS+ are not supported" for every code; `nis_sperror_r` copies it into the caller's buffer (truncated, terminated) and returns the buffer (`NULL` for no buffer); `nis_perror` prints `<label>: <text>` to stderr; `nis_lerror` does nothing (no syslog socket); the `nis_print_*` printers print nothing (no stub ever yields an object to print); `nis_freeresult` frees what it is given (every result comes from a stub, one block); `nis_freenames`, `nis_freeservlist`, `nis_freetags`, `nis_free_directory`, `nis_free_object`, `nis_free_request`, `nis_destroy_object`, `__free_fdresult` do nothing (no stub returns their objects, and freeing a caller-built object could free what its owner frees again); `yp_unbind`, `nis_ping`, `__nisbind_destroy` no effect. No restore option (security, as D-29.4/D-29.5). Test: `crates/core/tests/s29_legacy_clauses.rs` `s29_2_c_0`; `placeholders::tests`. |
